role: President of the Committee for Basic People's Defence and Social Self-Protection
organization: League of Socialist Youth of Slovenia (Zveza socialistične mladine Slovenije, ZSMS)
description: Appointed in 1982. According to the government's official biography he was dismissed early because of his critical writings on the Yugoslav People's Army (JLA); Wikipedia states that his re-election was blocked in 1984.

organization: Mladina, Problemi and Časopis za kritiko znanosti
description: According to his official biography he wrote critical articles on political pluralism, conscientious objection, Yugoslavia's cooperation with dictatorships and the use of Slovene in the armed forces, and was active in the new peace and environmental movements.

Co-founded a small computer company that, according to his official biography, served as a technical base for dissident activities, including printing the working paper for a democratic Slovenian constitution.

According to Wikipedia he became editor-in-chief of the weekly shortly after his release from prison following the JBTZ trial and held the post until May 1990, a month after his election to parliament.

role: Vice-president, later President of the Party Council
organization: Slovenian Democratic Union (Slovenska demokratična zveza, SDZ)
description: Took part in founding one of the first opposition parties in Slovenia, a member of the DEMOS coalition that won the first free elections in 1990 (official biography, Wikipedia).

organization: Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia (1990), then National Assembly (Državni zbor)
description: According to his official biography he has been elected to parliament at every parliamentary election since 1990, most recently on 22 March 2026. Members of the government cannot sit in the National Assembly, so his seat passes to a substitute while he holds government office. In 2014 the National Assembly declared that his mandate had ended with the final judgment in the Patria case; the Constitutional Court stayed that decision and unanimously annulled it on 11 June 2015.

organization: Government of the Republic of Slovenia (governments of Lojze Peterle and Janez Drnovšek)
description: According to his official biography he oversaw the formation of Slovenia's first armed forces which, together with the police, fought the Yugoslav People's Army in June and July 1991. Prime Minister Janez Drnovšek dismissed him in March 1994 in the wake of the Depala vas affair (dates from Wikipedia).

organization: Slovenian Democratic Party (Slovenska demokratska stranka, SDS; until 2003 the Social Democratic Party of Slovenia, SDSS)
description: Elected party president in May 1993, succeeding Jože Pučnik, and re-elected ever since. Under his leadership the party grew from 3.34% of the vote in 1992 to first place in 2004 and 2018, and came a close second in 2026.

role: Head of the Slovenian parliamentary delegation
organization: North Atlantic Assembly (now the NATO Parliamentary Assembly)
description: Led the National Assembly's delegation while Slovenia was seeking NATO membership (official biography).

organization: Government of the Republic of Slovenia (government of Andrej Bajuk)
description: Served in the short-lived centre-right government of Andrej Bajuk; his official biography credits him with preparing the second action plan for full NATO membership and gives his term as June to October 2000, while Wikipedia dates it until the next government took office on 30 November 2000.

organization: Government of the Republic of Slovenia
description: Coalition of the SDS, New Slovenia, the Slovenian People's Party and DeSUS. Slovenia adopted the euro on 1 January 2007 and joined the Schengen area on 22 December 2007. The government won a confidence vote it had called on 19 November 2007; the SDS came second at the September 2008 election and Borut Pahor succeeded him.

role: Prime Minister presiding over the Slovenian Presidency of the Council of the EU; chair of the European Council
organization: Council of the European Union / European Council (Slovenian Presidency)
description: Slovenia was the first member state from the 2004 and 2007 enlargements to hold the Council presidency; according to his official biography he chaired two European Council meetings and four summits with non-EU countries.

organization: Government of the Republic of Slovenia
description: Coalition of the SDS, Gregor Virant's Civic List, DeSUS, the Slovenian People's Party and New Slovenia, formed after the early election of December 2011. It pursued austerity during the euro-area crisis; the coalition broke up after the anti-corruption commission's January 2013 report on his assets, and on 27 February 2013 the National Assembly designated Alenka Bratušek as Prime Minister in a constructive vote of no confidence (55–33).

organization: Government of the Republic of Slovenia
description: Formed after the resignation of Marjan Šarec, with New Slovenia, the Modern Centre Party and DeSUS. The term was dominated by the COVID-19 pandemic and by disputes with EU institutions over media freedom and the European Public Prosecutor's Office. The SDS lost the April 2022 election to Robert Golob's Freedom Movement.

role: Prime Minister presiding over Slovenia's Presidency of the Council of the EU
organization: Council of the European Union (Slovenian Presidency)
description: Slovenia's second presidency of the Council of the EU, held during his third term (official biography).

organization: Government of the Republic of Slovenia
description: Elected by the National Assembly on 22 May 2026 by 51 votes to 36; the government, with 15 ministers (five fewer than its predecessor), took office on 4 June 2026. The coalition agreement for 2026–2030 was signed by the SDS, New Slovenia, the Slovenian People's Party, Fokus and Anže Logar's Democrats (43 of 90 seats); Resni.ca supports the government without formally joining it.
